Subject: AlderBio model profile + committed pool sizing

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we want to move the conversation to concrete sizing for a reserved pool tied to our Q1 contract. A few specifics to help your sizing:

- Primary model: a 62B parameter open transformer (v1.2) with a 64k context target for recall-heavy retrieval flows.
- Typical request: 5–8k input tokens + ~1k generation on average per call.
- Peak concurrency target for the committed pool: 35 steady concurrent requests with bursts up to ~70 for short windows.
- Expected qps for the pool baseline: ~20 sustained qps.
- We expect to use quantized weights if accuracy loss is <1% — curious on tradeoffs for 4-bit vs 8-bit for this model.

I've attached our inference profile csv (AlderBio-inference-profile.csv) with token-length CDFs and serve-time traces. Can you map this to an estimated GPU footprint (NVLink pod sizing or single-GPU counts) and highlight risk areas (KV cache, sequence headroom, fallback plan if quant introduced quality regressions)?

We are targeting a signed commitment by 11/01 if the sizing and pricing align.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of ML Ops
AlderBio

Hi Samantha — thanks for the profile, this is exactly what we need. I'm attaching a quick initial sizing matrix (initial-sizing-matrix.xlsx) that maps your percentiles to approximate GPU counts and pod shapes. High level notes up front: 

- Baseline option (conservative): 8 x H100-80GB-equivalent GPUs in a reserved pod tuned for 64k KV (we assume KV stored in GPU memory with offload headroom). This supports ~30 steady concurrent requests at your 5–8k avg input + 1k output with safety headroom.
- Cost-optimized option (aggressive quant): 12 x A10-equivalent or 16 x 80GB-quantized-GPU mix using 4-bit weight quantization + KV compression. This reduces GPU count but raises risk of small-but-measurable regressions around long-context attention caching.
- KV cache: for 64k context we estimate ~18–24GB of KV per request in-heap (model and KV vary by precision). With shared KV caching and prefix reuse you may cut that by ~30% for retrieval-heavy flows.

A couple of quick clarifying Qs so we can refine to a firm pod recommendation:
1) What fraction of requests do you expect to have full 64k history versus trimmed contexts? The CSV shows a long tail but if 95% are <16k that changes the optimal tiling.
2) Do you require cross-request KV stickiness (i.e., reuse between sessions) or can we assume per-request cold-start?
3) Any hard constraints on on-prem vs cloud region or preferred GPU families?

If you prefer, we can run a short validation benchmark on your sample traces (we'll need temporary access to the profile or a sanitized subset).

I'll loop in Soojin for quant/KV overhead specifics.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: AlderBio model profile + committed pool sizing — quant & KV detail

Thanks Karthik / Samantha — I pulled the profile and ran a few internal microbenchmarks against the model family with simulated 64k KV. Key findings (short):

- Memory per request (approx):
  - FP16 baseline: ~42–48GB (weights+activation+KV working set)
  - 8-bit symmetric quant (weight only): ~28–32GB (activation and KV still dominate)
  - 4-bit quant (AWQ / QLoRA style): ~20–24GB (additional CPU-side dequant costs and small throughput variance)

- KV cache specifics:
  - Full KV for 64k context (no compression): ~18–22GB extra per active sequence on top of the model footprint.
  - With prefix-sharing (retrieval-heavy flows) and 2:1 compression heuristics we get effective KV down to ~9–11GB for many requests.

- Throughput tradeoffs: 4-bit gives the best memory reduction but increases kernel complexity; expect ~10–15% variance in tail latency vs 8-bit on long-context runs. If you need hard SLOs (<150ms tail), 8-bit is the safer default for now.

Recommendation matrix (practical):
- Safety commit (SLA-focused): 10 x 80GB GPU nodes (H100-equivalent) with reserved KV headroom and automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model variant for extreme tails.
- Cost-optimized commit (price-driven): 14 x 80GB-quantized GPUs (4-bit) + aggressive KV prefix caching. Include a canary phase where we validate quality on a set of prompts (we can automate A/B evals for the 1% quality window).

Operational notes: the biggest risk is cross-request KV stickiness; if you require per-session state retention across many concurrent users we'll need separate pool partitioning and higher overall GPU counts.

I'll attach a short internal memo with the microbench outputs.

Soojín Lee
PM, Performance & Serving
Redwood Inference

2) Commit: subject to canary results, target a reserved pool equivalent to your Safety commit (10 x 80GB GPUs) for Q1 with a 12-month commitment window. We will include an SLA clause for tail latency and a rollback path if quality regressions exceed 1.5% per eval set.
